I tested the valve-monitor feature on the Ventura platform, and it works fine in our environment.
I retested this patch on the latest codebase, and it works as expected.
I don't see the inventory item in your below testing?
This is related PR section. For inventory item, refer to related PR [1],i.e. https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77415.
Tested again on the Ventura platform, and it works fine.

Overall in support of this feature, I do wonder why we're making a new application, given that going GPIO -> Dbus interface is essentially the same thing Leak detectors do, just with a few different interfaces.  was that considered?

The GPIO common code is already part of common code/class in https://github.com/openbmc/dbus-sensors/blob/master/src/GPIOInterface.cpp. This common code gets used both in leak detection and valve-monitor. This service mainly holds the app/daemon specific logic. Moreover, the leak detection and valve monitor are two different features, hence they have been added as two different services.

Marking this as resolved with above reasoning. Let me know if you still have any questions here.

> This service mainly holds the app/daemon specific logic

right, but this application specific logic seems trivially different.  Why do we need a whole new application for this?  Yes, I understand the GPIO code itself is common.

I believe only one design would use GPIO for valve control, this would be a binary open/close. But we potentially could see other designs where the valve control could be continuous using a DAC/ADC (Where valve could be at various sates of open from 0% to 100%), thus potentially having this as a distinct service with GPIO being just one backend.

@ed@tanous.net Amithash is correct. There’s a follow-up use case where we set the valve flow rate via a DAC and read back feedback via an ADC. Since this introduces a new hardware interface (separate from the existing GPIO-based valve monitor), it seems cleaner to model it as a separate service.
Let me know if you have any other questions; otherwise, I’ll mark this as resolved.
when I looked through the code, 90+% looks like boilerplate for a new application.  How is that "cleaner"?

> This service mainly holds the app/daemon specific logic. Moreover, the leak detection and valve monitor are two different features, hence they have been added as two different services.


We generally separate by transport, not by "feature". Note that all pmbus devices go through psusensor, all temp sensors go through hwmontempsensor (although they're both hwmon/sysfs for their interface, so arguably should be combined at some point).

I really don't like creating applications just for the heck of it.  If there's a lot of valve-specific logic, I could see this needing to be it's own application, but at a code level it's just libgpio -> dbus and could be common, even if main just calls two different paths, right?

> > This service mainly holds the app/daemon specific logic. Moreover, the leak detection and valve monitor are two different features, hence they have been added as two different services.
> 
> 
> We generally separate by transport, not by "feature". Note that all pmbus devices go through psusensor, all temp sensors go through hwmontempsensor (although they're both hwmon/sysfs for their interface, so arguably should be combined at some point).

I’m referring to the device type. In dbus-sensors, most services are structured this way (e.g., psusensor, fan, adc, hwmon-temp), and i am following the same pattern here.

> 
> I really don't like creating applications just for the heck of it.  If there's a lot of valve-specific logic, I could see this needing to be it's own application, but at a code level it's just libgpio -> dbus and could be common, even if main just calls two different paths, right?

I’m not creating a new application solely for the reasons above. You may have missed the other key rationale I mentioned earlier, so I’m restating it here: there’s a follow-up use case for an Analog Valve where the valve flow rate is set via a DAC and the feedback is read via an ADC. This AnalogValve will be part of the same service.
Marking this comment as resolved based on the reasoning above, as there are no further comments.

I suspect it would be better to split these into two objects, OutputInterface and InputInterface.  Having a single object and tracking a bool to determine what mode its in seems like more trouble than it's worth in terms of interfaces (evidence by now needing to add if(!inputMode) below.)
Done
As written, don't all of these need inputMode checks?  See comment above about splitting up things.
Done
You have two interfaces that inherit from associations?
One is a association for control interface and other is for value interface. Refer to my reply here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82574/comment/e2188fa6_0f5e7d75/.
Why are these two separate with multiple inheritance?  SHouldn't they both be in the same object?

Because one is a control interface and other is a value interface and each of these interface reside on a different objectPath (value path vs control path), hence so.  

This is similar to whats being already done for other implementations in dbus-sensors https://grok.openbmc.org/search?full=%22%2Fxyz%2Fopenbmc_project%2Fcontrol%2F%22&defs=&refs=&path=%2Fopenbmc%2Fdbus-sensors%2Fsrc&hist=&type=&xrd=&nn=1&si=full&searchall=true&si=full.
This clang warning is related to the style for auto generated PDI definitions which are being overridden here. NOLINTNEXTLINE here is to skip that warning.
this seems like we should specify the type of state, why aren't we?
This is overriding the PDI generated definitions, which has the similar signature. Refer to https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/master/example/calculator-aserver.cpp#L50 for example.

1. We generally don't use bools
2. We probably want to define this as "asserted" in some fashion.  Maybe the same way we do inverted GPIOs elsewhere?  As written this isn't very clear what it does.

> 1. We generally don't use bools
> 2. We probably want to define this as "asserted" in some fashion.  Maybe the same way we do inverted GPIOs elsewhere?  As written this isn't very clear what it does.

I suppose you are referring to OpenControlValue. I had explicitly named it so it reflects whats the value required to open the valve. Similar concept of value gets used in https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/schemas/gpio_presence.json#L24. 

FYI: This has been already been approved and merged in EntityManager https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/82310.
Marking this as resolved since there are no further questions.

@spinler@us.ibm.com did you not see these when you merged 82310?

Yes, there are counter examples, that we know to be mediocre.  For new things, lets use enumerations please.
Sure, for future use cases will use enumerations.

Not entirely sure what's being asked?  These comments didn't exist when the EM commit was merged last August.  If I missed some best practice that wouldn't surprise me but maybe we should get them in writing. 

As this would be the only user of the schema anyway, it would be easy enough to make changes to it without affecting others.

Is there a more specific type we can use here?  The valves I know of are Assert open, deassert close.  Obviously this one is more complicated, so lets give it a name.  I'm not sure what that would be though.  If you have an example datasheet for one of these values, I can help suggest more things.

> Is there a more specific type we can use here? The valves I know of are Assert open, deassert close.  Obviously this one is more complicated, so lets give it a name.  I'm not sure what that would be though.  If you have an example datasheet for one of these values, I can help suggest more things.

What more specific type are you looking for? I have named it similar to other GPIO based EM schemas, for example, GPIOLeakDetector, GPIODeviceDetect.
FYI: This has been already been approved and merged in EntityManager https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/82310.
Marking this as resolved since there are no further questions.
sensors/valve_open isn't a namespace, and this isn't a sensor under the normal definitions.  What that path discussed somewhere?

Redfish has defined valve as a sensor https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/schema/dmtf/json-schema/Sensor.v1_11_1.json#L164.

This has already been added to the sensors namespace in PDI. Please refer to https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/82304.

I am marking this as resolved. Please let me know if you still got any questions.
